Following yesterday's release of public betas for macOS 27, iPadOS 27, iOS 27, and other updates unveiled at WWDC26, Apple is now rolling out the first wave of public beta firmware for AirPods Max 2, AirPods Pro 3, AirPods Pro 2, and AirPods (4th generation). Here's what you need to know.

First AirPods public beta firmware is now available

At WWDC26 last month, Apple announced several new AirPods features that will arrive alongside iOS 27 and other upcoming operating system updates.

These include customizable EQ sound settings that let users personalize their AirPods listening experience, as well as expanded GymKit support that enables AirPods Pro 3 users to sync heart rate data through their iPhone.

Apple is also debuting beta firmware for AirPods Max 2 for the first time, which can be enrolled via a device running iOS 27 or macOS 27.

Following yesterday's launch of the first public betas for iOS 27 and Apple's other upcoming operating systems, the company has now released the first public beta firmware updates for the following AirPods models:

  • AirPods Max 2
  • AirPods Pro 3
  • AirPods Pro 2
  • AirPods Pro 2（USB-C）
  • AirPods（第四代）
  • AirPods（第四代，主動降噪）

The release build number for AirPods firmware version 9.0.314 is 9A5314b, matching last week's developer beta.

Installing AirPods beta firmware

Below is Apple's official tutorial for enrolling eligible AirPods in the firmware beta program:

Enable beta updates — For Mac running macOS 27 beta or later: To enable AirPods beta, connect your AirPods to your Mac via Bluetooth settings. Go to System Settings > Bluetooth, then click (i) next to your AirPods. In the AirPods settings menu, scroll down to find "AirPods Beta Updates." Use the toggle to enable beta software updates. For iPhone and iPad running iOS 27 beta or later: To enable AirPods beta, connect your AirPods to your iOS device. Go to Settings > Bluetooth, then tap (i) next to your AirPods. Apple notes that once users flip on the "AirPods Beta Updates" toggle, "firmware updates will be installed automatically when your AirPods are in their charging case and near a paired iPhone or Mac."
